How an agent run ended

Source: R/run-ending.R
RunEnding.Rd

An AgentResult carries a RunEnding in its ending property. It says how the run ended and holds only what that ending has, so you can act on an ending without reading the stop_reason string:

  • RunEndingAnswered: the model finished its answer.

  • RunEndingStopped: someone or something stopped the run. by says who, and reason is the reason they gave.

  • RunEndingLimit: the run reached a limit. reason names it, and field, actual and limit give the UsageLimits field, the figure reached and the figure allowed, when the limit has them.

  • RunEndingCutOff: the provider cut the answer short. finish_reason says why. The result's stop_reason is still "complete", since the run was not stopped.

  • RunEndingFailed: an error ended the run. error is the condition, when there is one, and phase says where it came from.

RunEnding is the parent class; use it to test for any ending with S7::S7_inherits(x, RunEnding). Agents create these values. You only need the constructors to build an AgentResult yourself, for example in a test.

Endings are read-only. Read a property with $ (a missing one gives NULL), @ or S7::prop().

Usage

RunEnding()

RunEndingAnswered()

RunEndingStopped(by, reason = NULL)

RunEndingLimit(reason, field = NULL, actual = NULL, limit = NULL)

RunEndingCutOff(finish_reason)

RunEndingFailed(reason = "error", error = NULL, phase = NULL)

Arguments

by

Who or what stopped the run: one of "caller", "hook", "permission", "approval", "parent", "delegation" or "abandoned".

reason

For RunEndingStopped(), the reason the stopper gave, or NULL. For RunEndingLimit(), the limit's stop reason, such as "request_limit". For RunEndingFailed(), the failure's stop reason, "error" by default.

field

The UsageLimits field that was reached, such as "max_requests", or NULL.

actual

The figure the run reached, or NULL. NA when it is unknown, as the cost is for "cost_unavailable".

limit

The figure the limit allowed, or NULL.

finish_reason

The provider's finish reason, as ellmer names it: one of "max_tokens", "context_window" or "content_filter".

error

The condition that ended the run, or NULL.

phase

Where the run failed, such as "initialization" or "stream", or NULL.

Value

A RunEnding object of the class named.

Which ending a stop reason gives

  • "complete": answered, or cut off when the last response's finish reason is "max_tokens", "context_window" or "content_filter".

  • "request_limit", "tool_call_limit", "input_token_limit", "output_token_limit", "total_token_limit", "cost_limit", "cost_unavailable", "tool_loop": a limit.

  • "error", "provider_error", "file_checkpoint_error" and the reasons a failed delegation or batch gives: failed.

  • Anything else: stopped. by is "caller" for $interrupt(), "hook" for a hook that stopped the run, "permission" for a denied call that asked to stop it, "approval" for a run waiting for an approval, "parent" for a subagent whose lead finished, "delegation" for a batch whose subagents were stopped, and "abandoned" for a stream nobody read to its end. A reason you pass to $interrupt() or return from a hook is kept in reason, and whoever gave it is credited in by, whatever the reason says.

See also

AgentResult

Examples

result <- AgentResult(response = "Done")
result$ending
#> <RunEndingAnswered>

stopped <- AgentResult(stop_reason = "interrupted")
S7::S7_inherits(stopped$ending, RunEndingStopped)
#> [1] TRUE
stopped$ending$by
#> [1] "caller"

RunEndingLimit("request_limit", field = "max_requests", actual = 5, limit = 5)
#> <RunEndingLimit>
#>   reason: request_limit
#>   field: max_requests
#>   actual: 5
#>   limit: 5
